notes: Rates and bracket widths are statutory and not indexed (2%/4%/5%; head of family uses the single schedule). No rate change has been enacted for 2026.

Standard deduction (2025 ADOR chart; 2026 chart not yet published) phases down as Alabama AGI rises above $25,999: single loses $25 per $500 to a $2,500 floor, MFJ $175 per $500 to $5,000, HoH $135 per $500 to $2,500. Modeled as a straight-line phase-down.
Alabama allows a deduction for federal income tax paid or accrued (Form 40, line 12; income tax only, not SE tax). Modeled using the estimated federal income tax.
Half of SE tax is not an adjustment to Alabama AGI. FICA and federal self-employment tax can instead be claimed as an Alabama itemized deduction (Schedule A, line 6); not modeled.
Dependent exemptions (amount depends on AGI), itemized deductions and credits are not modeled.

seDeduction.note: Alabama computes its own AGI (Form 40 Part II adjustments), and the deductible half of SE tax is not on the list; SE tax is deductible only as an itemized deduction.

seHealthInsurance.note: Form 40 page 2, Part II, line 7 allows the self-employed health insurance deduction.

retirementContributions.note: Form 40 Part II, line 2 allows payments to a Keogh retirement plan and self-employment SEP deduction (self-employed qualified plans).

qbi.note: Alabama does not start from federal taxable income and has no QBI-equivalent deduction.

localIncomeTax.note: Some Alabama municipalities and counties (for example Birmingham) levy local occupational license taxes on wages and/or business license taxes; they are administered locally, not by ADOR, and are not modeled.

estimatedTax.threshold: Required if you expect to owe at least $500 of Alabama tax for 2026 after withholding and credits.
estimatedTax.safeHarbor: No penalty if withholding plus credits are at least the smaller of 90% of 2026 tax or 100% of 2025 tax (110% if 2025 Alabama AGI was over $150,000, or $75,000 married filing separately).
estimatedTax.form: Form 40ES (Individual Estimated Tax) or My Alabama Taxes online

businessCosts.llcFormationFee: $200 Secretary of State filing fee for a domestic LLC Certificate of Formation (a name reservation is filed first and carries its own fee).
businessCosts.annualReportFee: None with the Secretary of State for LLCs. Pass-through entities file the Business Privilege Tax return (Form PPT) with ADOR only when the privilege tax exceeds $100.
businessCosts.franchiseOrMinimumTax: Business Privilege Tax on LLCs and disregarded entities: $0.25 to $1.75 per $1,000 of Alabama net worth. For tax year 2026, entities whose tax would be $100 or less have no filing requirement and owe nothing (the former minimum tax no longer applies). Maximum $15,000.
businessCosts.grossReceiptsTax: None at the state level. Local business licenses (which may be based on gross receipts) are set by cities/counties.
